title: An image tool faced an investigation into sexualised content risks
eventPeriod: Grok deployment on X; investigation announced January 2026
summary: The European Commission opened a DSA investigation into X’s handling of risks from Grok, including manipulated sexual images and possible child sexual abuse material.
aiRole: The investigation concerns image-generation features and how their deployment could spread illegal content.
affected: People depicted in manipulated images and users exposed to harmful material. This record gives no victim count.
outcome: The Commission announced an investigation into risk assessment and mitigation. This source records an opening, not a final decision or penalty.
limitation: The source does not establish every alleged image, a finding against every user, or the present status of all related proceedings. UK investigations and civil lawsuits are not counted as separate cases here. No abusive images are displayed.
lesson: Before releasing an image tool, test misuse risks and provide effective reporting and removal routes.

title: An AI image lawsuit ended with a narrow, mixed ruling
summary: The UK High Court partly upheld Getty’s trademark claim against Stability AI, while rejecting its secondary copyright infringement claim.
aiRole: The dispute concerned Stable Diffusion and generated watermarks, alongside copyright allegations about the models.
affected: The parties and creative contributors whose rights were at issue. No damages amount or victim total is inferred.
outcome: The judge described the successful trademark findings as historical and very limited. Training and output copyright claims had been abandoned; secondary infringement failed.
limitation: This is the UK judgment, not a decision on every US claim or on AI training worldwide. The dropped training claim was not a ruling that all training was lawful or unlawful. This record does not establish the current appeal position.
lesson: Read the actual outcome. Training rights, generated outputs and trademarks can raise different questions.

title: Voter profiling began with deceptive data collection
technology: Data analytics and voter profiling; specific AI method not established
eventPeriod: Facebook data collection and voter profiling; FTC action in 2019
summary: The FTC found that Cambridge Analytica used deceptive practices to collect data from tens of millions of Facebook users for voter profiling and targeting.
aiRole: This is a related data-analytics ethics case. The cited FTC account does not identify a particular AI model or demonstrate its effect on election results.
affected: Facebook users whose information was collected. The source describes tens of millions; this record does not substitute an exact 87-million count.
outcome: The FTC issued an opinion and final order against the company, including restrictions on privacy-related misrepresentations.
limitation: The finding concerns deceptive data practices. It does not prove that AI changed the election result or that the 2016 election was a single technical AI incident. Facebook’s separate penalties are not assigned to Cambridge Analytica.
lesson: Check consent and data provenance before using personal information to profile or target people.

title: Age rules automatically rejected qualified job applicants
eventPeriod: Recruitment practices described in the EEOC lawsuit
summary: The EEOC said hiring software automatically rejected women aged 55 or older and men aged 60 or older, affecting more than 200 qualified US applicants.
aiRole: Programmed age-screening rules. The source does not establish a machine-learning model.
affected: Older applicants for remote tutoring work in the United States.
outcome: A $365,000 settlement provided compensation and measures against discriminatory hiring, with EEOC monitoring for at least five years.
limitation: This is a related automation case and a settlement, not a trial verdict or proof that AI independently learned discrimination.
lesson: Automating a discriminatory rule does not make the decision fair.

title: Welfare debt failures led to calls for accountable automation
eventPeriod: Robodebt scheme from 2015; Commission report in July 2023
summary: The Commission’s founding document acknowledged harm from Robodebt and an invalid debt demand. Its final report recommended safeguards for automated government decisions.
aiRole: Related government automation case. The report’s recommendations address review, transparency and scrutiny of algorithms; no LLM role is established.
affected: People affected by welfare debt assessment and recovery.
outcome: The report recommended plain-language explanations, clear review routes, independent scrutiny and monitoring for fairness and bias.
limitation: Recommendations are not proof that reforms were implemented. This record does not establish individual criminal responsibility, compensation totals or a current legal status for every proceeding.
lesson: Automating a process does not remove the need for lawful evidence and review.

title: Artists challenged how image models used their work
entity: Andersen and other artists / Stability AI and others
technology: AI image generation and training data
eventPeriod: US artists’ lawsuit; August 2024 dismissal-stage ruling
summary: Artists alleged that image-generation companies used their work without permission. An August 2024 court order let copyright claims proceed while dismissing other claims.
aiRole: The allegations concern training images and the operation of Stable Diffusion and related image products.
affected: Artists bringing the claims. This record gives no proven infringement or affected-artist total.
outcome: Copyright claims survived dismissal. DMCA claims were dismissed with prejudice; unjust-enrichment claims could be amended. Other claims had different outcomes.
limitation: Surviving dismissal is not a finding that infringement occurred. This records the August 2024 order, not the present status of the litigation or a final ruling on AI training.
lesson: Check rights before using creative work. Separate an allegation from a court’s final finding.
